articles.title: Goldman Sachs offloads Rs 169 Cr worth Eternal shares; BofA Securities buys
articles.description: Goldman Sachs has sold 53.37 lakh shares of Eternal, the parent company of Zomato and Blinkit, for Rs 168.67 crore through a block deal. BofA Securities bought the same number of shares on October 15. According to exchange data, Goldman Sachs sold 53,37,584 shares at Rs 316 each. BofA Securities purchased the shares at the same price. The transaction accounted for around 0.05% of Eternal's paid-up equity. The transaction comes weeks after large investors offloaded nearly Rs 3,265 crore worth of Eternal shares through bulk deals on August 31. BNP Paribas Financial Markets sold 5.09 crore shares worth Rs 1,670.86 crore, while Integrated Core Strategies (Asia), an affiliate of Millennium Management, sold 4.86 crore shares for Rs 1,593.96 crore. Eternal reported revenue from operations of Rs 20,211 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 7,167 crore in the year-ago period. Its net profit rose to Rs 92 crore from Rs 25 crore a year earlier. However, profit declined from Rs 174 crore in the March quarter. For FY26, the company's revenue from operations increased to Rs 54,364 crore from Rs 20,243 crore in FY25, while net profit fell to Rs 366 crore from Rs 527 crore. Eternal operates Zomato's food delivery business and Blinkit, its quick commerce platform. Blinkit competes with Swiggy Instamart and Zepto in India's quick commerce market, where companies are expanding their store networks to improve delivery capacity. Eternal shares are currently trading at Rs 323.6 (as on 09.37 AM) with a total market capitalization of Rs 3,11,947 crore.

Singapore’s non-oil exports jumped about 68% Geopolitics and oil US President Donald Trump told Newsmax that he would not use nuclear weapons against Iran and did not expect US ground troops to be sent into the country. He said, however, that the US may have to strike Pickaxe Mountain, an underground site near Natanz linked to Iran’s nuclear programme. The comments largely restated earlier positions, and Trump said last week that the US would not attack Iran before next month’s midterm elections. Separately, there were unconfirmed reports of possible launches of anti-ship ballistic missiles, anti-ship cruise missiles and drones towards port anchorages at Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah or Jebel Ali in the United Arab Emirates, or nearby areas of the Strait of Hormuz. The reports had not been verified at the time of writing. Oil prices edged only slightly lower over the session. FX and gold Gold traded around $25 higher. Several large Indian mutual funds, including Kotak, UTI and HDFC, halted bulk gold ETF subscriptions ahead of the festive season, reportedly after a nudge from SEBI, removing a seasonal support for gold as India seeks to shield the rupee. The US dollar eased slightly ahead of remarks from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh. Central banks Warsh declined to signal the Fed’s next move, saying he does not believe in saying what he might do at meetings for the rest of 2026. Speaking at an IMF session in Bangkok, he said the world has broadly conformed to the Fed’s expectations since its September rate hike. He described the October and December meetings as the crystallising moments for judging output, employment and inflation. He also said AI is likely to boost demand before it delivers supply-side gains. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack warned that if an inflationary mindset takes hold among households and businesses, the Fed may need to act more aggressively. She said businesses are facing significant input cost pressures and that financial conditions do not currently appear restrictive. Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said second-round effects from high energy prices have been subdued so far, but that it is too early to form a firm view. He described above-target UK inflation as enormously frustrating and said Middle East news is the biggest factor moving UK government bond yields. Markets have been pricing a high chance of a Bank of England rate rise on 5 November. Companies Moody’s changed its outlook on Nike to negative and affirmed its A2 rating, citing a turnaround taking longer than it had expected. The agency expects Nike’s revenue and earnings to decline through the fiscal year ending May 2027 and into fiscal 2028. Tesla unveiled its long-delayed next-generation Roadster, which uses thrusters developed with SpaceX to flip and land in mid-air. Reservations require $50,000 upfront, the price has not been confirmed, and production is due to start in 2028, years after deliveries were first promised for 2020. Asia data Singapore’s non-oil domestic exports rose about 68% in September from a year earlier, well above the roughly 32% expected in a Reuters poll and a sixth straight month of growth above 20%. The gain was driven mainly by non-electronics, chiefly ship and boat structures, though electronics exports also surged. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: Sensex, Nifty trade lower in early deals; IT shares buck trend
articles.description: Domestic equity benchmark indices traded lower on Friday, tracking mixed global cues, while information technology (IT) shares supported the market with gains. In early deals, Sensex was trading 0.29 per cent or 221.89 points lower at 74,093, hitting an intraday low. Similarly, Nifty recorded an intraday low of 22,942, down 0.24 per cent or 55.19 points. Earlier in the day Sensex opened 0.03 per cent or 25.47 points higher at 74,341.08 against its previous close of 74,315.61. While the 50-scrip basket began the trading session at 23,065.10, up 0.29 per cent or 67.75 points from its previous close of 22,997.35. In morning trade, Nifty IT, Nifty Media, Nifty PSU Bank and Nifty Metal surged up to 1.59 per cent. In contrast, Nifty Oil & Gas, Nifty MidSmall IT & Telecom and Nifty FMCG declined up to 0.86 per cent. Meanwhile, realty and auto sectoral indices were also trading lower, while pharma, cement, healthcare and private bank saw marginal declines. According to market experts, India has significantly outperformed other markets this week with 668-point gains in Nifty 50 in the last three days. The outperformance is driven by a weakening AI trade, expectations of major changes in LTCG taxation in the coming Budget, and positive fallout from Q2 results that have been better than expected so far. They further noted that good results from IT majors and positive management commentary have led to a smart 9 per cent revival in the IT index, contributing to the resilience of the Nifty."Q2 results of telecom, banking, automobiles and metals like copper, aluminium and zinc are expected to be impressive and provide fundamental support to the market," they added."Another positive development is the sharp decline in the US 10-year bond yield to 5.07 per cent. This, along with strength in the rupee, can restrain FII selling to some extent," according to the experts. However, FIIs are likely to continue selling so long as the 10-year yield remains above 5 per cent and Brent trades above $100. While maintaining a 23,200-23,600 view, analysts expect mean reversion moves while below 23,070, given the sharp rise in the previous session. Dips are expected to find buying interest as long as they do not stretch beyond 22,780. On global cues, Asian equities traded higher in early hours, mirroring US markets. The S&P 500 closed 0.33 per cent higher after recovering from early losses, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq ended flat, up 0.08 per cent.
